 News › Exams News › FMGE Admit Card 2026 Released! Download FMGE October Exam Hall Ticket @nbe.edu.in FMGE Admit Card 2026 Released! Download FMGE October Exam Hall Ticket @nbe.edu.in
 Jasleen Taneja Updated: Oct 28, 2026, 08:10 IST FMGE October 2026 Admit Card Out FMGE Admit Card 2026 : National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences released FMGE October 2026 admit card the official website. Candidates can download their hall tickets from nbe.edu.in. The exam will be conducted on October 31, 2026, in computer-based test mode.
 Candidates should download their FMGE October 2026 admit cards and check all details printed on them for its accuracy. The details shared are candidate's name, roll number, exam date, reporting time and exam centre.
 The admit card is an important document for entry to exam hall. Noone shall be allowed to write the exam without it. Candidates should carry a printed copy of the hall ticket. They must follow all instructions mentioned on it.
 Steps to download the FMGE October 2026 Admit Card
 Candidates can download FMGE admit card online. The steps to access and save hall ticket are shared below:
 Visit the official website at nbe.edu.in .
 Go to examinations section.
 Select Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE).
 Look for admit card link for October 2026 session.
 Click on link to open candidate login page.
 Enter login credentials.
 Select FMGE October 2026 admit card download option.
 Check details printed on admit card.
 Download hall ticket.
 Take a clear printout of admit card to carry to exam centre.
 Direct Link - Download FMGE Admit Card 2026 
 FMGE October 2026 Admit Card: Important Dates
 Candidates can see important dates for FMGE October 2026 exam here:
 Event Date 
 FMGE exam city intimation slip October 20, 2026 
 FMGE admit card release October 27, 2026 
 FMGE October 2026 examination October 31, 2026 
 FMGE October 2026 result (expected) November 30, 2026 
 FMGE Admit Card 2026: Exam Pattern Overview
 The test is conducted twice a year as a computer-based test (CBT). The question paper comprises 300 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) divided into two parts of 150 questions each, with each part allocated 150 minutes of testing time. There is no negative marking for incorrect answers.
